title: Image alt text repeats the text next to it
summary: An image's alt text matches the link or button text beside it, so screen readers say it twice. Use an empty alt on the image.
problem: An image inside a link or button has alt text identical to the visible text next to it, such as a cart icon with alt="Shopping cart" beside the words "Shopping cart". A screen reader announces the same phrase twice.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users hear the same words twice for every such control, which slows them down when they move through a menu or toolbar. Sighted users are not affected.
steps: Find images placed next to text that says the same thing. The scan result shows the exact markup.
Set the image's alt to an empty value (alt="") so the screen reader skips the image and reads only the visible text.
Keep the visible text as the name of the link or button.
If the image says something the text does not, keep a short alt that adds that information.
before: Shopping cart
after: Shopping cart
whyItMatters: This is a recommended practice, not a WCAG failure. Removing the repeat makes menus and toolbars quicker to move through with a screen reader and keeps the spoken name of each control clean.
howToCheck: Select the link or button in the browser accessibility inspector and read its Name. If the same phrase appears twice, the image alt text duplicates the visible text.
